```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(corrplot)
```

```{r}
its_electric_df <- read.csv("data_hourly.csv")

head(its_electric_df)
```

```{r}
glimpse(its_electric_df)
```
```{r}
its_electric_df %>% distinct(ID)
```


```{r}
its_electric_df %>% nrow()
```
13.5 million rows total

```{r}
its_electric_df %>% distinct(Experiment_price_NOK_kWh)
```


```{r}
its_electric_df %>% summarise(na_count = sum(is.na(Experiment_price_NOK_kWh)))
```
11.98 million NA values in Experiment_price_NOK_kwh

```{r}
its_electric_df %>% summarise(blank_count = sum(Experiment_price_NOK_kWh == "", na.rm = TRUE))
```


```{r}
its_electric_df %>% distinct(Price_signal)
```

```{r}
its_electric_df %>% summarise(blank_count = sum(Price_signal == "", na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r}
its_electric_df %>%
  mutate(
    signal_absent = is.na(Price_signal) |
      trimws(as.character(Price_signal)) == "",
    price_absent = is.na(Experiment_price_NOK_kWh)) %>%
  count(signal_absent, price_absent)
```

```{r}
its_electric_df <- its_electric_df %>%
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))

its_electric_df %>%
  group_by(Participation_Phase) %>%
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    households = n_distinct(ID),
    first_date = min(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_date = max(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    distinct_dates = n_distinct(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_consumption = sum(is.na(Demand_kWh)),
    missing_price = sum(is.na(Experiment_price_NOK_kWh)),
    .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#removing Phase 1 data for now.
its_electric_df2 <- its_electric_df %>%
  filter(Participation_Phase == "Phase_2")

glimpse(its_electric_df2)
```

```{r}
its_electric_df2 %>%
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    households = n_distinct(ID),
    demand_missing_val = sum(is.na(Demand_kWh)),
    no_demand = sum(Demand_kWh == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    neg_demand = sum(Demand_kWh < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(Demand_kWh, na.rm = TRUE),
    med = median(Demand_kWh, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(Demand_kWh, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(Demand_kWh, na.rm = TRUE))
```


```{r}
#Looking into electricity consumption
its_electric_df2 %>%
  filter(Demand_kWh == 0) %>%
  count(ID, name = "no_demand_hrs", sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
its_electric_df2 %>%
  filter(Demand_kWh == 0) %>%
  count(From, name = "houses_with_zero", sort = TRUE)
```


```{r}
its_electric_df2 %>%
  filter(Demand_kWh == 0) %>%
  mutate(norway_hour = lubridate::hour(lubridate::with_tz(lubridate::ymd_hms(From, tz = "UTC"),"Europe/Oslo"))) %>%
  count(norway_hour, name = "zero_readings", sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
ggplot(its_electric_df2, aes(x = Demand_kWh)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, fill = "lightblue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Phase 2 hourly electricity consumption", x = "Hourly consumption (kWh)",
    y = "Number of household-hour observations") +theme_minimal()
```
Note: This is hourly consumption.
Follows along with the basic statistics above, consumption is right-skewed. 
scale goes out that far because there's at least one data point at 22.62.

Investigate daily, possible comparison to US values. 
Source: https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/use-of-energy/electricity-use-in-homes.php
US: Average 10500 kWh per year = Average of 28.8 per day.

Note: This average per day is for the whole calendar year, and not specifically for winter. As such it isn't a great comparison. 

```{r}
daily_df <- its_electric_df2 %>%
  group_by(ID, Date) %>%
  summarise(
    hours_recorded = n(),
    missing_hours = sum(is.na(Demand_kWh)),
    daily_kWh = sum(Demand_kWh),
    .groups = "drop")

daily_df %>% count(hours_recorded, missing_hours)
```

```{r}
daily_df %>%
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    households = n_distinct(ID),
    demand_missing_val = sum(is.na(daily_kWh)),
    no_demand = sum(daily_kWh == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    neg_demand = sum(daily_kWh < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(daily_kWh, na.rm = TRUE),
    med = median(daily_kWh, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(daily_kWh, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(daily_kWh, na.rm = TRUE))
```


```{r}
ggplot(
  filter(daily_df, hours_recorded == 24, missing_hours == 0),
  aes(x = daily_kWh)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "lightblue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Phase 2 daily household electricity consumption", x = "Daily consumption (kWh)",
    y = "Number of household-day observations") + theme_minimal()
```
Roughly the same pattern for daily consumption. 


```{r}
hourly_pattern <- its_electric_df2 %>%
  mutate(norway_hour = lubridate::hour(lubridate::with_tz(lubridate::ymd_hms(From, tz = "UTC"), "Europe/Oslo"))) %>%
  group_by(norway_hour) %>%
  summarise(mean_kWh = mean(Demand_kWh, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
glimpse(hourly_pattern)
```

```{r}

ggplot(hourly_pattern, aes(x = norway_hour, y = mean_kWh)) +
  geom_line(color = "lightblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  labs(title = "Average daily electricity consumption pattern: Phase 2",
    x = "Hour of day (Norway local time)",
    y = "Mean household consumption (kWh during hour)") + theme_minimal()
```

Makes sense that Electricity usage would decrease over night as that's when I'd assume people are sleeping. The spike from 1500 to 1930 is interesting though. 

```{r}
its_electric_df2 %>%
  count(Price_signal, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
signal_pattern <- its_electric_df2 %>%
  filter(!is.na(Price_signal), trimws(Price_signal) != "") %>%
  mutate(norway_hour = lubridate::hour(lubridate::with_tz(lubridate::ymd_hms(From, tz = "UTC"),"Europe/Oslo"))) %>%
  group_by(Price_signal, norway_hour) %>%
  summarise(mean_kWh = mean(Demand_kWh, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
glimpse(signal_pattern)
```

```{r}
ggplot(signal_pattern, aes(x = norway_hour, y = mean_kWh)) +
  geom_line(color = "lightblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "red", size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Price_signal) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 4)) +
  labs(title = "Hourly consumption by price signal: Phase 2",
    x = "Hour of day (Norway local time)",
    y = "Mean household consumption (kWh during hour)") +theme_minimal()
```
These graphs show that the average for each price signal follows roughly the same pattern, some are lower like A_5 and some are higher like P_5. Unsure how relevant these would be without comparing to the control households but interesting nonetheless. 

```{r}
#Moving on to add temperature
temperature_pattern <- its_electric_df2 %>%
  filter(!is.na(Temperature), !is.na(Demand_kWh)) %>%
  mutate(temp_band = floor(Temperature)) %>%
  group_by(temp_band) %>%
  summarise(mean_kWh = mean(Demand_kWh), observations = n(),.groups = "drop")

glimpse(temperature_pattern)
```

```{r}
ggplot(temperature_pattern, aes(x = temp_band + 0.5, y = mean_kWh)) +
  geom_line(color = "lightblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(size = observations), color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Electricity consumption by outdoor temperature: Phase 2",
    x = "Outdoor temperature (°C)",
    y = "Mean hourly household consumption (kWh)",
    size = "Household-hours") + theme_minimal()
```

Not a very linear graph, so consumption doesn't change at a strictly linear rate with temperature. Also interesting to see the groupings compared to outdoor temps, they are to be expected but interesting to see. 

```{r}
participants <- readr::read_csv("participants.csv")

phase2_groups <- its_electric_df2 %>%
  left_join(participants %>%
      select(ID, Region, Control_Price_Phase2), by = "ID")

glimpse(phase2_groups)
```

```{r}
a5_times <- phase2_groups %>%
  filter(Price_signal == "A_5") %>%
  distinct(Region, From)
glimpse(a5_times)
```

```{r}
a5_comparison <- phase2_groups %>%
  semi_join(a5_times, by = c("Region", "From")) %>%
  filter(Price_signal == "A_5" | Control_Price_Phase2 == "Control group") %>%
  mutate(comparison_group = if_else(Control_Price_Phase2 == "Control group","Control","A_5"),
    norway_hour = lubridate::hour(lubridate::with_tz(
        lubridate::ymd_hms(From, tz = "UTC"),
        "Europe/Oslo"))) %>%
  group_by(comparison_group, norway_hour) %>%
  summarise(mean_kWh = mean(Demand_kWh, na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop")

```


```{r}
ggplot(a5_comparison, aes(x = norway_hour, y = mean_kWh, color = comparison_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 2)) +
  labs(title = "A_5 versus control: average hourly consumption",
    subtitle = "Matched region and timestamps",
    x = "Hour of day (Norway local time)",
    y = "Mean household consumption (kWh during hour)",
    color = "Group") + theme_minimal()
```
